Highlights from the presentation of the FY 2026/27 Budget Statement by Cabinet Secretary for the National Treasury, Hon. John Mbadi, delivered on 11th June 2026.

#BETA #DeliveringThePlan

The Finance Bill 2026 seeks to strengthen the efficiency, fairness and administration of the tax system while supporting the implementation of the FY 2026/27 Budget.

I met the Departmental Committee on Finance and National Planning during their retreat in Kiambu County to clarify key proposals contained in the Finance Bill, 2026 and provide additional information on the policy rationale underpinning the proposed measures.

Among the proposals is the exemption of dialysers used in kidney dialysis treatment from VAT, a measure that will help reduce the cost of healthcare and improve access to life-saving treatment for Kenyans.

The Bill also seeks to simplify tax compliance, expand the tax base, reduce revenue leakages, rationalise tax expenditures, modernise tax administration and enhance domestic revenue mobilisation in a manner that supports businesses, creates jobs and promotes economic growth. 

Through broadening participation in the tax system and improving compliance, the proposed measures aim to ensure a more equitable distribution of the tax burden while generating sustainable revenues to finance national development priorities.

I commend the Committee, under the leadership of Hon. Francis Kuria Kimani (MP Molo), for its diligence and commitment throughout the consideration of the Finance Bill, particularly in undertaking public participation across the country. The views and recommendations received from Kenyans are critical in shaping a fair, responsive and inclusive tax policy framework.
Meeting with the National Assembly Departmental Committee on Finance and National Planning, Kiambu County.

The Budget for Financial Year 2026/27, anchored on the theme “Sustaining the Bottom-Up Economic Transformation Agenda for Resilient and Inclusive Growth amid Global Uncertainty,” is designed to accelerate economic growth, expand opportunities for youth and MSMEs, strengthen social protection, enhance climate resilience and improve the livelihoods of all Kenyans under the leadership of H.E. the President, Dr. William Samoei Ruto.

The Budget allocates KSh 4.82 trillion towards sustaining economic transformation, creating jobs, supporting businesses and strengthening service delivery across the country. It builds on the gains made under the Bottom-Up Economic Transformation Agenda while laying a strong foundation for resilient, inclusive and sustainable growth.

It prioritises investments in education, healthcare, agriculture, affordable housing, infrastructure, digital transformation, national security and social protection, while maintaining a clear path towards fiscal consolidation and debt sustainability.

Key allocations include KSh 784.5 billion for Education, KSh 531.3 billion for Energy, Infrastructure and ICT, KSh 177.2 billion for Health, KSh 135.7 billion for Affordable Housing, KSh 111.7 billion for Agriculture, and KSh 502 billion to support County Governments in delivering essential services to wananchi.

Today, Kenya has taken another important step in advancing the Bottom-Up Economic Transformation Agenda with the presentation of the FY 2026/27 Budget at the Parliament Buildings in Nairobi by the Cabinet Secretary for the National Treasury, Hon. John Mbadi. 

This Budget reaffirms the Government’s commitment to sustaining economic transformation, creating opportunities for all, strengthening resilience and building a more prosperous and self-reliant Kenya.

The Kaptagat Forest Ecosystem is one of Kenya’s most important water towers, supporting water security, environmental sustainability, agricultural productivity and livelihoods across the North Rift region. 

Today, we briefed the Head of Public Service, Mr. Felix Koskei on preparations for the 10th Edition of the Kaptagat Integrated Conservation Programme (KICP), to be held on 11th July 2026 at Penon Forest Block, Keiyo South, and graced by H.E. the President William Samoei Ruto. 

As we mark 10 years of conservation, restoration and community empowerment, we are preparing for a landmark celebration that will showcase the transformative impact of KICP in restoring degraded landscapes, strengthening environmental stewardship and improving livelihoods.

I welcomed the newly appointed Commissioner General of the Kenya Revenue Authority (KRA), Mr. Adan Mohamed to the National Treasury.

We are working closely with KRA to mobilise domestic revenue, promote efficiency, broaden the tax base, tap into emerging tax streams in the digital economy and create an enabling business environment that supports investment, job creation and economic growth.

We have reached agreement on the implementation of the Kenya–U.S. Health Cooperation Partnership, a five-year programme valued at US$1.6 billion. The programme will support disease surveillance and outbreak response, laboratory systems strengthening, health commodities, frontline health workforce transition and digital health systems.

U.S. companies operating in Kenya continue to make a significant contribution to job creation, skills development, investment and economic growth, underscoring the strong economic ties between our two countries.

I received Susan Burns, Chargé d’Affaires at the U.S. Embassy Nairobi, who paid a courtesy call on me at the National Treasury. We reaffirmed our shared commitment to deepening economic cooperation, strengthening trade and investment ties and advancing the longstanding partnership between our two countries.

Later in the day, I visited community members and Community Forest Associations (CFAs) at Kaptarkok, Kiptulos and Chepsamo in Keiyo South, where we held a public engagement on community empowerment and development issues.

I commended the CFAs for their exemplary stewardship of the forest, which has contributed significantly to the restoration and conservation of the Penon Forest block.

In recognition of these efforts, Penon Forest Station will host the 10th Edition of the Kaptagat Integrated Conservation Programme (KICP) on 11th July 2026 under the theme “10 to 20: Restore. Sustain. Transform.”

The late Mzee Nicholas Kigen Rono will be remembered for his humility, wisdom and unwavering commitment to his family, faith and community.

Congratulations to Michelle and Michael on taking this important step in their journey together. I wish the couple God’s blessings, happiness and a successful marriage as they begin this new chapter of their lives.

The Kenya–China partnership continues to play an important role in advancing Kenya’s development agenda through transformative infrastructure, healthcare and economic cooperation initiatives that support sustainable growth and improve the wellbeing of our people.

I received H.E. Amb. Haiyan Guo, Ambassador of the People’s Republic of China to Kenya, who paid a courtesy call on me at the National Treasury to discuss areas of mutual interest and further strengthen the longstanding relations between our two countries.

The Ambassador updated me on the planned upgrading of Londiani Hospital and Baringo County Referral Hospital under ongoing Kenya–China cooperation. These projects, together with others in the pipeline, will improve access to quality healthcare, strengthen service delivery and contribute to Kenya’s socio-economic transformation.

On this World Environment Day, we are reminded that the health of our planet and the prosperity of our people are deeply interconnected.

As we confront the challenges of climate change, pollution and environmental degradation, we must strengthen our commitment to responsible waste management, ecosystem restoration and the sustainable use of natural resources.

Together, let us protect our natural heritage and build a cleaner, greener and more resilient future for generations to come.

Competitive markets are critical in driving economic growth, protecting consumers, promoting innovation and creating opportunities for businesses to thrive.

As we implement the Bottom-Up Economic Transformation Agenda (BETA) and the Fourth Medium-Term Plan, we recognise that fair competition is not merely a regulatory objective but also a key economic policy tool for attracting investment, lowering the cost of doing business, strengthening consumer welfare, and creating jobs.

The Government continues to strengthen coordination across Ministries, Departments and Agencies, as well as county governments, to accelerate the implementation of national priorities, development projects and the delivery of better services to citizens.

This morning, I joined colleagues at the monthly PSs Meeting, chaired by Felix Koskei, Chief of Staff and Head of the Public Service, at the Kenya Advanced Institute of Science and Technology (Kenya-AIST) in Konza Technopolis, Machakos County.

The choice of Kenya-AIST at Konza Technopolis as the venue reflects the Government’s commitment to advancing science, technology, innovation, and research as key drivers of economic transformation while positioning Kenya as a regional hub for higher learning, innovation, and cutting-edge scientific research.

Strong internal audit systems are critical in safeguarding public resources, improving service delivery and strengthening public confidence in Government institutions.

We are in the process of finalising the Draft Public Finance Management (Amendment) Bill, 2026, which seeks to strengthen the independence, professionalism and effectiveness of internal audit systems, while the Zero Fault Audit Initiative continues to promote a culture of compliance, accountability and excellence in public financial management.

Today at the National Treasury, I received the leadership of the Institute of Internal Auditors - IIA Kenya led by Ms. Lilian Wangechi (Chairperson) and Dr. Joyce Omina (CEO), who paid a courtesy call to discuss ongoing reforms aimed at enhancing internal audit functions across Government.

We will continue working closely with professional bodies and key stakeholders, including the Office of the Auditor-General, to strengthen governance systems, enhance transparency and promote accountability in the management of public resources.

I was joined by Dr. Sammy Kimunguyi, the Internal Auditor-General at the National Treasury.

Welcomed Mr. Robert Tchaidze, the incoming International Monetary Fund (IMF) Resident Representative for Kenya, who paid a courtesy call at the National Treasury as he begins his assignment in the country.

I also bid farewell to Mr. Selim Cakir, the outgoing IMF Resident Representative for Kenya, as he concludes his tour of duty. I commend him for his contribution in strengthening the partnership between Kenya and the IMF and wish him success in his future engagements.

Kenya will continue to work closely with the IMF to advance our economic and fiscal reform agenda and strengthen macroeconomic stability.

The African Trade and Investment Development Insurance (ATIDI) continues to play a critical role in promoting trade, investment, and economic development across the continent through innovative risk-mitigation and investment-support solutions.

As a founding Member State of ATIDI and host of its headquarters since its establishment in 2001, Kenya remains committed to supporting the institution’s mandate and strengthening regional economic integration.

Today, I met with Mr. Manuel Moses, Chief Executive Officer of ATIDI, who briefed me on the preparations for the 26th ATIDI Annual General Meeting (AGM), which Kenya will host from 30th June to 3rd July 2026 in Nairobi.

The AGM will provide an important platform for strengthening partnerships, promoting trade and investment, and advancing Africa’s shared development agenda, while also showcasing Kenya’s position as a regional financial and investment hub.

The late Eng. Anne Jepkokei Cheboi lived a life defined by service, leadership and a deep commitment to uplifting others.

Throughout her career and community engagements, she inspired many young people, particularly girls pursuing careers in science, technology and engineering. She was also an integral member of the Kaptagat Integrated Conservation Programme (KICP), where she made a significant contribution to environmental conservation and community empowerment initiatives.

Personally, I have lost a friend and a relative who served as my deputy in our larger family. Her warmth, generosity and commitment to others will remain a lasting inspiration to many of us.

Today, I joined her family, friends and colleagues at Illula, Ainabkoi, Uasin Gishu County, for her final send-off.

We celebrate a life well lived, marked by professionalism, compassion, resilience and an unwavering desire to make a positive difference in society.

May her soul rest in eternal peace.

The Mau Forest Complex is one of Kenya’s most vital natural resources and the largest afro-montane forest ecosystem in East Africa. As the country’s largest and most important water tower, it provides critical ecological services. It is the source of 12 major rivers that drain into Lake Victoria and eventually flow through the Nile Basin.

This invaluable natural resource must be protected and conserved for present and future generations. Today in Nairobi, I joined my colleague, Dr. Eng. Festus Ngeno (PS Secretary Environment & Climate Change) and other stakeholders in committing to the conservation and restoration of the Mau Forest.

The forest supports livelihoods for communities within its ecosystem, sustains biodiversity and contributes to national development. Its restoration is also critical to achieving Kenya’s ambitious target of planting 15 billion trees by 2032.

The Government is committed to supporting our content creators and the creative economy to ensure young people continue to benefit from their talents, innovation and enterprise.

They continue to use creativity and talent to entertain, educate and positively influence society. Their work has earned recognition both locally and internationally through digital content creation and comedy.

I commend Team Strong not only for creating impactful content but also for supporting vulnerable members of society through various community initiatives, especially by leveraging their platforms and opportunities to reach out to those facing medical challenges and other hardships.

The FY 2026/2027 Budget prioritises key sectors to stimulate economic growth and improve livelihoods, allocating KSh 379.5 billion to BETA priorities. This includes KSh 131.4 billion for infrastructure, KSh 122.5 billion for social sectors, KSh 59.5 billion for production and finance, KSh 46.1 billion for governance and public administration, and KSh 20.1 billion for land and natural resources.

To strengthen devolution and enhance service delivery across the country, the Budget has provided KSh 495.5 billion in transfers to county governments, alongside allocations to the Equalisation Fund, NG-CDF, and the National Government Affirmative Action Fund. 

The Budget also places strong emphasis on youth empowerment, enterprise development and job creation through strategic investments, including over KSh 22.6 billion for youth programmes, over KSh 21 billion for internship programmes, KSh 8.8 billion for affordable credit to MSMEs, KSh 110 billion for affordable housing, KSh 18 billion for fertiliser subsidy and KSh 2 billion for seeds subsidy.

Kenya continues to strengthen its engagement with The Commonwealth in key areas, including debt management, economic development, trade and investment cooperation.

Through this shared partnership, the National Treasury continues to benefit from technical assistance and capacity development in debt recording, reporting, risk analysis and sustainable financing through the Commonwealth Meridian Debt Management System.

The Menengai Geothermal Projects continue to demonstrate Kenya’s commitment to expanding clean, reliable and affordable energy through strategic public-private sector collaboration.

Today, together with my colleagues in the PPP Committee, we inspected the Menengai Geothermal Project in Nakuru County to assess the progress of the ongoing geothermal power development being implemented through a unique partnership model where the Geothermal Development Company (GDC) undertakes geothermal exploration and de-risks the steam fields before supplying steam to Independent Power Producers (IPPs) for power generation.

The development is being undertaken in phases, with the first phase targeting 105MW through three 35MW power plants by Sosian Menengai Geothermal Power Limited, Globeleq Menengai Limited and OrPower Twenty-Two Limited.

The Gilgil–Nakuru–Mau Summit Road Project is a key transformative infrastructure initiative aimed at improving connectivity and easing traffic congestion along the busy Northern Corridor, which has for many years experienced perennial traffic jams for motorists travelling to western Kenya, neighbouring Uganda and beyond.

This afternoon, together with my colleagues in the PPP Committee, we inspected the ongoing project works along the corridor being implemented by the Kenya National Highways Authority (KeNHA) and Shandong Hi-Speed Road and Bridge International Engineering Co., Ltd (SDRBI).

The project includes the development of a six-lane dual carriageway between Gilgil and Nakuru, a four-lane elevated carriageway within Nakuru Town, and a four-lane dual carriageway between Nakuru and Mau Summit, alongside the construction of toll stations along the corridor.

Construction activities are progressing well, with most of the required equipment already mobilised to support the works. The project is expected to be completed by June 2027 and will significantly improve transport efficiency, enhance road safety and boost local and regional trade and economic growth.

The Ministry of Defence continues to make significant progress in the construction of housing units under the PPP framework on a Build-Transfer basis, aimed at addressing housing constraints within the KDF fraternity.

We carried out an inspection of the PPP housing project at Gilgil Barracks in Nakuru County, with construction works now at 80 percent completion under the KDF Housing Programme.

The programme will provide 3,069 houses for service members across Roysambu, Nanyuki, Lanet, Gilgil and Mariakani Barracks. Construction across all five sites is progressing concurrently, with the Roysambu project already completed 500 units, which were commissioned last year.

The Government, through the Ministry of Defence and its partners under the PPP framework and the Affordable Housing Programme, continues to implement transformative housing projects that provide dignified accommodation for military personnel while also creating employment opportunities for many Kenyans.

The Rironi–Gilgil (A8) & Rironi–Maai Mahiu–Naivasha (A8 South) Road Project under the Public Private Partnership (PPP) framework is a transformative infrastructure initiative aimed at improving connectivity, easing traffic congestion and enhancing trade and economic growth along the Northern Corridor.

The project is being undertaken by a consortium of China Road and Bridge Corporation (CRBC) and the National Social Security Fund under the Design, Finance, Build, Operate, Maintain and Transfer model.

This morning, together with my colleagues on the PPP Committee, we inspected the ongoing project works along the corridor.

The project scope includes the development of a dual carriageway of approximately 59 kilometres between Rironi and Naivasha, a six-lane dual carriageway of approximately 22 kilometres between Naivasha and Gilgil, and a dual carriageway of approximately 22 kilometres from Rironi to Maai Mahiu, alongside rehabilitation and upgrading works between Maai Mahiu and Naivasha. The project will also include the construction of toll stations along the A8 and A8 South corridors.

The contractor has mobilised additional teams to accelerate works, with excavation, spoil material hauling and fill layer processing already progressing well and expected to be completed by June next year.

We remain committed to transforming Kenya from a developing country into a first world economy under the aspirations and leadership of H.E. the President William Samoei Ruto.

Today, I engaged residents of Kapchemutwa Ward, where we distributed 30,000 high-value coffee seedlings to support export growth, value addition, and improved household incomes for farmers.

We also issued high nutrition Pakchong grass cuttings to empower farmers through enhanced livestock and dairy production.

These interventions align with the Government’s agenda of strengthening Kenya’s export sector through increased agricultural productivity, market access and promotion of high-value crops.

I was accompanied by Prof. Grace Cheserek, Deputy Governor of Elgeyo Marakwet County, Hon. Steve Cheruiyot, area MCA & Majority Leader in the Elgeyo Marakwet County Assembly, and Hon. Christopher Cheboiboch, MCA Emsoo Ward.

This morning, I visited the Emsoo Dam water distribution project in Keiyo North Constituency, aimed at improving access to water for residents of Emsoo Ward in both the upper and lower valley areas through enhanced water infrastructure for domestic use, micro-irrigation, and livestock.

The Government has and will continue to provide funding through the Kerio Valley Development Authority (KVDA) to undertake major rehabilitation and expansion works at Emsoo Dam to boost water capacity and enhance long-term sustainability.

The planned interventions include dam desilting, excavation works to increase storage capacity, embankment improvement and erosion protection works, extension of the water supply pipeline network, fencing and environmental conservation activities, and the installation of water tanks at strategic locations to improve distribution and access.

We also planted indigenous trees as part of ongoing efforts to restore and protect the Elgeyo Forest Block ecosystem.

Deeply saddened by the passing of Eng. Anne Cheboi, who was recently appointed as a Member of the PPP Tribunal at the National Treasury. She was a distinguished electrical engineer and accomplished professional with over 15 years of experience in the ICT and Energy sectors, where she championed quality engineering, renewable energy, climate action and transformational projects across the country.  

Eng. Cheboi was also a strong, committed, and full-of-life member of the Kaptagat Integrated Conservation Programme (KICP), of which I am the Patron.

We have lost a dependable colleague, a committed professional, and a true champion of transformative development, whose contribution to sustainable energy, environmental stewardship, and community impact will remain unforgettable.

My heartfelt condolences to her family, friends, colleagues and the entire KICP fraternity during this difficult time.

May her soul rest in eternal peace.

The occasion also marked the launch of the School’s Strategic Plan 2026–2030, which will serve as an important roadmap in nurturing responsible future leaders and strengthening the transformative role of education in society.

We were joined by Members of Parliament Hon. Joseph Makilap (Baringo North), Hon. Timothy Kipchumba (Marakwet West) and Hon. Gideon Kimaiyo (Keiyo South).

We were joined by Hon. Timothy Kipchumba (MP Marakwet West), Hon. Gideon Kimaiyo (MP Keiyo South), among other leaders.

Highlights from my engagements at the G7 Finance in Paris, where I represented Kenya and advanced our priorities on the global issues shaping our economy and future. #G7 #ParisFrance

Terrorism financing remains a global threat that requires coordinated international action and long-term commitment, stronger partnerships and enhanced intelligence sharing. 

Kenya has undertaken significant steps to strengthen its Anti-Money Laundering and Counter Financing of Terrorism framework through legal, regulatory and institutional reforms aimed at addressing emerging terrorism financing threats, such as new technologies, and aligning the country’s financial integrity system with international standards.

Participated in the 5th No Money for Terror Conference in Paris, France, during a panel discussion on obstruction of financial strategies used by terrorist groups relying on territorial controls. 

H.E. Emmanuel Macron, President of France, who closed the meeting, reaffirmed France’s commitment, under its G7 Presidency, to redoubling efforts to deliver concrete results in addressing global economic and financial challenges.

Communiqué for the G7 Finance Ministers and Central Bank Governors’ consultations with Finance Ministers and Central Bank Governors from Brazil, India, Kenya and South Korea held on May 19, 2026 in Paris, France.

Together with Dr. Kamau Thugge, Governor of the Central Bank of Kenya, we participated in the G7 Finance Ministers and Central Bank Governors’ Meeting in Paris, France, where Kenya was invited alongside India, Brazil and South Korea to contribute to discussions on global economic and financial challenges.

Kenya reaffirmed the need for stronger global cooperation to address emerging economic challenges, including the impact of geopolitical tensions and developments around the Strait of Hormuz, which continue to exert pressure on supply chains, energy prices, trade corridors, and financial stability, particularly on developing economies.

We also seized the opportunity to urge G7 members to support reforms towards a more inclusive and balanced global financial architecture that promotes equitable access to affordable financing, supports investment and industrialisation, strengthens resilient supply chains, and responds to the realities and development priorities of African countries.

Met with Kristalina Georgieva, Managing Director of the International Monetary Fund, at the G7 Finance Ministers and Central Bank Governors’ Meeting in Paris.

We appreciate the IMF’s continued support for Kenya’s economic reform agenda as the country undertakes fiscal consolidation measures to address fiscal challenges while promoting sustainable economic growth.

Arrived in Paris, France, with Dr. Kamau Thugge, the Governor of the Central Bank of Kenya, to represent Kenya at the G7 Finance Ministers and Central Bank Governors’ Meeting, where discussions will focus on global imbalances, international partnerships and solidarity, and the macroeconomic impact of rising energy prices resulting from the ongoing conflict in the Middle East.

I will also represent my Cabinet Secretary, Hon. John Mbadi, at the 5th No Money for Terror Ministerial Conference as we continue advancing global cooperation in combating terrorism financing and strengthening international financial integrity.

National Infrastructure Funds (NIF) are a transformative financing vehicle designed to mobilise long-term capital for the development and management of critical infrastructure, including highways and railways, air and seaports, power generation, transmission and distribution, irrigation systems, and agribusiness infrastructure.

By attracting capital from diverse sources, including pension funds, sovereign wealth funds, private equity, and development finance institutions, NIFs enable investors to participate in the growth potential of the infrastructure sector while supporting large-scale, long-term national projects.

Globally, National Infrastructure Funds have reshaped investment landscapes by accelerating the shift from debt heavy public financing toward blended, investment led models that are sustainable, efficient, and market driven.

Through the NIF, Kenya seeks to mobilise KSh 5 trillion by unlocking domestic savings, strategically monetising mature public assets, democratising ownership through capital markets, and deploying national savings for development. Proceeds from privatisation will be ring-fenced and invested through the Fund to preserve and grow national value.

This is an innovative and sustainable approach to financing commercially viable infrastructure that supports growth, jobs, and long-term prosperity.

Moody’s upgrades Kenya’s sovereign credit rating to B3 and revises outlook to stable. 

Global ratings agency Moody’s Ratings has upgraded Kenya’s long-term local and foreign currency sovereign credit rating to B3 from Caa1 and revised the outlook to stable. This reflects a reduction in near-term default risk and improved financial fundamentals.  ￼

Moody’s highlighted stronger external liquidity, significantly higher foreign exchange reserves, and a narrower current account deficit as key factors supporting the upgrade. These improvements have strengthened Kenya’s ability to meet external obligations and reduced refinancing pressures.  ￼

The stable outlook signals that Moody’s expects these gains to be sustained over the medium term, backed by ongoing economic reforms and better access to international capital markets.  ￼

Overall, this upgrade represents a notable vote of confidence in Kenya’s macroeconomic management and financing strategy.

Automating external debt payments is a major step in modernising Kenya’s public financial management. This fully digital system will improve efficiency, transparency, and accountability, and is set to go live in February 2026. #BETA #DeliveringThePlan

Automation of external debt payment marks a major milestone in the modernisation of Kenya’s public financial management systems.

We are fully automating the external debt payment platform, which is now ready for deployment under the Treasury Single Account framework. This reform will significantly enhance efficiency, transparency, accountability, and governance in the management of Kenya’s external debt obligations.

The system integrates the Meridian Debt Management System with the Central Bank of Kenya exchange rates system, IFMIS, Exchequer requisition and the Office of the Controller of Budget approval process, enabling seamless generation, approval, and execution of debt payment instructions, while transitioning fully from manual, paper-based processes to secure digital workflows.

I was briefed by the project team on the implementation progress, with the automation scheduled to go live on 2nd February 2026. A parallel run for one month will be undertaken to ensure a smooth, controlled, and risk-mitigated transition.

We are strengthening Kenya’s energy transmission through smart Public Private Partnerships, mobilising private capital, reinforcing the grid, and delivering reliable, affordable power to drive national growth. 

#BETA #DeliveringThePlan

Public Private Partnerships are a key focus of our infrastructure strategy, enabling the mobilisation of private capital and technical expertise while maintaining fiscal discipline and protecting public value.

We have taken an important step in strengthening Kenya’s energy architecture by signing the National Transmission Infrastructure Public Private Partnership with Africa50 and PowerGrid, with the Kenya Electricity Transmission Company Limited (KETRACO) as the Contracting Authority. This project reinforces our transmission backbone, which is essential for reliable, affordable and sustainable electricity to support economic growth, regional development and national resilience.

The investment covers two critical transmission corridors. The 400 kV Lessos Loosuk line strengthens system stability, provides an alternative evacuation route for Lake Turkana wind power and supports geothermal development in the Baringo Paka Silali area. The 220 kV Kibos Kakamega Musaga line introduces high-voltage supply to Western Kenya, improves network adequacy, and significantly reduces technical losses and load shedding.

This project will enhance the integration of renewable energy, support industrial and commercial activity and improve power supply for households, schools, hospitals and businesses.

Public sector wage bill management is a key focus in Kenya’s efforts to strengthen fiscal sustainability and ensure efficient use of public resources.

Met the International Monetary Fund (IMF) Fiscal Affairs Department team that has concluded a Wage Bill Mission. The team, led by Ignatius de Bidegain and joined by the IMF Resident Representative in Kenya, Mr. Selim Cakir, held extensive consultations with key institutions in the public sector to analyze expenditure trends and evaluate ongoing reforms across Government Ministries, Departments and Agencies (MDAs). The Mission’s consultations also included Independent Commissions, the Council of Governors and Public Sector Trade Unions.  ￼

The mission provided a preliminary assessment of wage bill trends, system efficiency, sector data, and employment practices across Ministries, Departments and Agencies, as well as County Governments. 

The insights gathered during this mission will support the Government of Kenya in developing evidence based policies to manage the public sector wage bill effectively. This will support evidence based policy reforms aimed at improving wage bill management, promoting accountability and reinforcing the Government’s commitment to prudent public financial management.

Kenya’s horticulture sector is a fundamental pillar of Kenya’s economy, generating approximately USD 1.2 billion annually, creating over 500,000 jobs, the majority of which are held by women, and driving rural transformation across the country.

I met with key buyers and stakeholders at the International Floriculture Trade Fair (IFTF 2025) in the Netherlands, where over 40 Kenyan companies are showcasing our vibrant flower industry. The Netherlands remains our largest export market, accounting for 43.3 percent of Kenya’s flower exports, followed by the United Kingdom at 17.1 percent and the broader European Union market.

The Kenya-EU Economic Partnership Agreement (EPA), which entered into force in 2024, guarantees duty and quota free access for Kenyan products to the entire EU market. It provides a stable and predictable framework for trade, investment, and sustainable development cooperation.

Our focus remains on finalizing and operationalizing the EPA Implementation Strategy, strengthening SPS and certification systems to sustain EU market compliance, deepening collaboration with Dutch and EU partners in logistics, innovation, and green technology, and promoting the Kenya Brand globally as a symbol of quality, sustainability, and resilience.

Participation in the Fair was spearheaded by the Kenya Flower Council under the leadership of its CEO, Mr. Clement Tulezi. I was joined by Amb. Anthony Mayo, Deputy Head of Mission at the Kenyan Embassy in The Hague, and Dr. Florence M’Kaibi, Agriculture Attaché at the Kenyan Mission in Brussels, Belgium.

The European Union accounts for a significant share of our exports in horticulture, floriculture, tea, and coffee. In 2024, Kenya’s exports to the EU rose to USD 1.56 billion, reflecting steady growth and deepening economic ties.

During my official working visit to Brussels, I held a bilateral meeting with Ms. Dora Correia, Director for Africa at the European Commission’s Directorate General for Trade (DG Trade), on the implementation of the Kenya EU Economic Partnership Agreement (EPA). The EPA provides duty and quota free access for Kenyan products to the EU market, promotes sustainable value chains, and creates opportunities for investment, industrial development, and green growth.

We are keen to leverage this Agreement to expand value addition and green manufacturing, strengthen trade facilitation and logistics systems, deepen cooperation on climate smart and digital trade, and foster joint ventures in agro processing, clean technology, and renewable energy.

The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) is a multilateral development bank that was established in 1991 to promote sustainable and inclusive market economies. 

Kenya acceded to the EBRD in  July 2025, becoming its 79th member, which marks a significant milestone in strengthening partnerships for green growth, infrastructure financing, and private sector development. The granting of Recipient Country status to Kenya on September 2025 has enabled EBRD to begin operations and investments in the Country.

This support has been directed to initiatives such as the programmes under the Water Services Trust Fund and the upgrading of Maternal and Newborn Units, valued at over KSh 3.4 billion.

The Mau Forest Ecosystem is one of Kenya’s most critical water towers, supporting livelihoods, agriculture, and biodiversity across the country and beyond. Its conservation cannot be overemphasized, as it remains central to our nation’s environmental and economic well being.

I joined H.E. President Dr. William Samoei Ruto at the Tree Planting Exercise in the Mau Forest Complex (Gacharage Forest Block), where the Government launched the Mau Forest Complex Integrated Conservation and Livelihood Improvement Programme (MFC ICLIP), a ten year initiative aimed at restoring 33,000 hectares of degraded forest land under the patronage of Dr. Eng. Festus Ng’eno, Principal Secretary for Environment and Climate Change.

This effort mirrors the transformative work we have advanced through the Kaptagat Integrated Conservation Programme (KICP), which celebrated its ninth anniversary in July this year. Through KICP, the restoration of the Kaptagat Forest ecosystem has been achieved by fostering strong community partnerships and promoting sustainable livelihood initiatives.

I commend the Ministry of Environment, Climate Change, and Forestry for adopting and scaling up this integrated model, as well as its replication across the country, as we work towards achieving H.E. the President’s target of 15 billion trees by 2032.

KENYA RAISES USD 1.5 BILLION  (Sh193.5 BILLION) AT LOWER COST AND PAYS OLD DEBT EARLY.

The Government has successfully raised USD 1.5 billion (Sh193.5 billion) from international investors and at the same time tendered to pay off the outstanding USD 1 billion of the 2028 Eurobond ahead of schedule.

This is the third such transaction since 2024, and it shows the Government’s firm commitment to managing debt more wisely, paying off loans on time, and protecting Kenyans from sudden repayment shocks.

The money was raised in two parts:

A 7-year bond of USD 750 million at 7.875%, and
A 12-year bond of USD 750 million at 8.8%,
together giving Kenya a better rate of 8.7%, which is 1% lower than what the country would have paid at the start of the year.

 By securing this deal, the Government has also smoothened and lengthened debt repayments, giving Kenya more breathing space in managing its finances.

The response from investors was very strong. The Government asked for USD 1.5 billion, but investors offered more than USD 7.5 billion  five times the amount needed.

Most of this support came from trusted international fund managers in the United States America and the United Kingdom, showing that the world has renewed confidence in Kenya’s economy.

This success means Kenya will spend less on interest, ease pressure on taxpayers, and keep the economy stable while creating room to fund development priorities such as roads, health, and education.

The Intergovernmental Budget and Economic Council (IBEC) serves as the key platform for consultation and coordination between the National and County Governments on fiscal and economic matters, ensuring coherence in budget policy, revenue sharing, and disbursement planning. It is chaired by H.E. the Deputy President, Prof. Kithure Kindiki.

At the 28th Ordinary Session of the Intergovernmental Budget and Economic Council (IBEC), held at the Deputy President’s Official Residence in Karen, I presented on behalf of the Cabinet Secretary for the National Treasury and Economic Planning, Hon. John Mbadi, highlighting the Budget Review and Outlook Paper (BROP), the status of FY2025/26 county disbursements, and updates on the County Governments Additional Allocations Act (CGAAA).

Our discussions centered on rationalizing expenditure, prioritizing completion of ongoing projects, enhancing budget credibility, and scaling up PPPs for development financing. We are also strengthening transparency through e-procurement, payroll consolidation, pension digitization, and the migration to accrual accounting and zero-based budgeting.

The National Government remains committed to protecting critical spending while implementing bold reforms to revive manufacturing through County Aggregation and Industrial Parks, lower the cost of power and capital, strengthen value chains, and entrench devolution. These measures will sustain macroeconomic stability, empower counties to deliver quality services, and unlock new opportunities for job creation and business growth.

Kenya’s Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) are the backbone of our economy, employing over 15 million Kenyans and contributing nearly 40% of GDP. Yet, they face a financing gap estimated at KES 2.5 trillion due to limited access to affordable credit.

In this regard, the National Treasury organized a high level breakfast meeting on the establishment of the Kenya Credit Guarantee Company (KCGC), a transformative initiative to unlock MSME financing. I represented my Cabinet Secretary, Hon. John Mbadi, in this forum that brought together key partners, including Paul Russo, Chairman of the Kenya Bankers Association (KBA) and Group CEO of KCB Group PLC, and Qimiao Fan, the World Bank Country Director for Kenya, alongside senior government officials, development partners, and financial sector leaders.

Building on the success of the Credit Guarantee Scheme (CGS) launched in 2020, which has already supported 4,315 MSMEs with KShs. 6.6 billion in credit across 46 counties, the new Company will scale this impact. With KES 3 billion seed capital from Government and strong commitment from banking fraternity, KCGC will reduce collateral barriers, attract private and development partner investments, and sustainably power enterprise growth. The Government will hold a minority shareholding of 25% in the Company to ensure greater efficiency, sustainable impact and benefit from a rich blend of expertise and governance structures.

This initiative will be a game changer in bridging the MSME financing gap, driving inclusive growth, and strengthening Kenya’s financial ecosystem under the Bottom Up Economic Transformation Agenda (BETA) and Vision 2030.

Strengthening Rural Financial Inclusion in Kenya.

The Rural Kenya Financial Inclusion Facility (RK FINFA), implemented by the National Treasury & Economic Planning in partnership with IFAD, is a USD 136 million programme that kicked off in 2022 as a six year project. The initial project counties are Bungoma, Busia, Embu, Kakamega, Kirinyaga, Kisii, Machakos, Meru, Nakuru, Nandi, Nyeri, Siaya, Tharaka Nithi and Trans Nzoia. These 14 counties, located in both Central Eastern and Western Kenya, were selected because they already host ongoing IFAD funded projects.

The mission will review progress, address challenges, and strengthen collaboration to ensure RK FINFA continues to deliver impact in line with the Bottom Up Economic Transformation Agenda (BETA), empowering farmers, women, and youth while building a more climate resilient rural economy.

In addition, updates were shared on the Equalization Fund, the County Government Additional Allocation Bill, and the macroeconomic and fiscal framework for the FY 2025/26 budget.

As the climate crisis continues to threaten food systems and rural livelihoods, today’s discussions marked another milestone in advancing the Integrated Natural Resources Management Programme (INReMP). Implemented with a KES 34 billion (USD 262.68 million) investment from the Government of Kenya, the International Fund for Agricultural Development (IFAD), the Green Climate Fund (GCF) and the Global Environment Facility (GEF), the programme will benefit ten counties across the Cherangany Hills and Mau West water towers — Elgeyo Marakwet, West Pokot, Trans Nzoia, Uasin Gishu, Nandi, Kakamega, Kericho, Kisumu, Homa Bay and Migori.

INReMP aims to improve the food, nutrition and income security of rural households within a sustainable and resilient ecosystem. Its development objective is to enhance integrated natural resources management, increase resilience to climate change and improve livelihoods, especially for women, youth and other vulnerable groups. The programme directly targets 407,176 vulnerable rural households (over 2 million people) through three core areas: community-led management of natural resources, ecosystem services and climate action; improved, inclusive and sustainable rural livelihoods; and strengthened policies and institutions for integrated resources management and rural coordination.

Together with the IFAD Country Director for Kenya, Mariatu Kamara, PS Kipronoh Rono (Agriculture) and PS Eng. Festus Ngeno (Environment and Climate Change), we reviewed progress on this transformative programme.

Importantly, we welcomed news of a potential additional grant cofinancing of KES 325 million (USD 2.5 million) from the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation under the Climate Smart Agribusiness Partnerships for Resilience (CSAPR) initiative. This will strengthen climate information systems in agricultural value chains, enabling farmers and agri MSMEs to access timely data that boosts productivity, resilience and profitability.

This growing confidence in INReMP underscores our shared commitment to mobilising resources, enhancing coordination and delivering meaningful change for Kenya’s smallholder farmers.

Launch of the Competition Authority of Kenya’s 4th Strategic Plan (2023/24–2027/28)

This morning, I joined stakeholders for the official launch of the Competition Authority of Kenya’s 4th Strategic Plan—an essential blueprint to promote competitive markets and safeguard consumer welfare.

Among CAK’s most transformative reforms has been its bold action against Abuse of Buyer Power. Following the 2019 amendments to the Competition Act, the Authority was empowered to protect small suppliers—particularly SMEs—after the collapse of Nakumatt and Uchumi, which left over Ksh 40 billion in unpaid supplier debts. A dedicated enforcement unit was established to restore fairness and rebuild confidence in the market.

The new Strategic Plan is well aligned with Vision 2030, MTP IV, and the Bottom-Up Economic Transformation Agenda (BETA), and is anchored on five strategic pillars: Competitive Markets, Consumer Protection, Research & Advocacy, Stakeholder Engagement, and Institutional Excellence.

As the National Treasury, we reaffirm our unwavering support for CAK through sound policy, adequate resourcing, and good governance.

Congratulations to Board Chair Mr. Shaka Kariuki, Director-General Mr. David Kemei, and the entire CAK team for this bold and forward-looking strategy.
